title: Automated Construction and Verification of Unextendible Product Bases
authors: Zicheng Han, Wanchen Zhang, Fei Shi, Xiande Zhang
abstract: Unextendible product bases (UPBs) are important structures in quantum information theory, with applications to completely entangled subspaces, bound entanglement, and local indistinguishability. Since many properties and applications of UPBs are closely related to their cardinalities, one of the central problems in the study of UPBs is to determine whether UPBs of prescribed sizes exist in a given multipartite system. In this paper, we introduce a SAT-assisted framework based on decompositions of the \(N\)-dimensional hypercube. We define \(O_N\)-tile decompositions and prove a tile-to-UPB theorem: every \(O_N\)-tile decomposition induces a UPB through a construction based on tile-wise Fourier product bases and a global stopper state. We then encode the search for such decompositions as a Boolean satisfiability (SAT) problem and use SAT solvers to generate explicit instances. In terms of verification, we also implement a UPB verification algorithm based on local orthogonality graphs and unsaturated subspaces. The algorithm can be used to determine whether an arbitrary finite set of product states forms a UPB. Using this framework, we obtain UPBs of several sizes in some tripartite and quadripartite systems, including sizes \(13,14,\ldots,23\) in \(\mathbb C^3\otimes\mathbb C^3\otimes\mathbb C^3\). Moreover, the small-dimensional instances obtained here can serve as seed UPBs for recursive constructions, leading to further examples in larger multipartite systems.
summary: This paper introduces a novel SAT-assisted framework to systematically construct and verify Unextendible Product Bases (UPBs) in multipartite quantum systems. By relating UPB existence to ON-tile decompositions of the hypercube, the authors provide an automated pipeline for generating explicit examples of these important structures. This advances the understanding of entanglement by providing concrete, verifiable examples of highly entangled subspaces.
main_problem: The central problem is determining the existence and constructing Unextendible Product Bases (UPBs) of specific sizes within multipartite quantum systems.
main_result: The authors established a tile-to-UPB theorem, providing an automated framework to generate explicit UPBs by solving combinatorial problems using SAT solvers.
method: They combine concepts from combinatorics (ON-tile decompositions of the hypercube) with computational tools (SAT solvers) and quantum information theory constructions (Fourier product bases).
model_or_system: The study concerns N-partite Hilbert spaces, $\mathcal{H} = \bigotimes_{i=1}^N \mathbb{C}^{d_i}$, where UPBs are sets of mutually orthogonal product states whose complement contains no non-zero product state.
key_observables: Cardinality (size) of the UPB; existence of ON-tile decompositions.
important_parameters: The dimensions $d_1, \dots, d_N$ of the local subsystems; the number of tiles $s$ in the decomposition.
main_assumptions: The construction relies on finding an ON-tile decomposition of the underlying hypercube structure.
figures_summary: Tables summarize known UPB sizes for small tripartite and quadripartite systems, showing new instances found through their systematic search.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, develops the SAT-assisted framework based on ON-tile decompositions, proves the tile-to-UPB theorem, implements a verification algorithm, and presents specific calculated examples of UPBs.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, systematic methods to construct highly structured quantum states (UPBs) that are crucial for understanding entanglement measures like bound entanglement in multipartite systems.
